message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | Deuterium is stable; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ≈ 12.3 yr). |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Weighted by natural isotope abundance. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Energy to remove the single valence electron. |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV | Requires breaking the nucleus‑electron bond. |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy released when an electron is added. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; boils near absolute zero. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at very low temperatures. |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Lightest gas; less dense than air. |
| **Molecular weight** | 2.01588 g mol⁻¹ (H₂) | Diatomic molecule under normal conditions. |
| **Molecular shape** | Linear (H–H) | Bond angle 180°. |
| **Bond dissociation energy** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy to break H₂ into two H atoms. |
| **Dipole moment** | 0 D (non‑polar) | Symmetric H₂ molecule. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive with many elements; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). | Forms covalent bonds readily; reacts with halogens, oxygen, etc. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable | Combustion produces water vapor: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. |
| **Color/odor/taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless | Invisible gas at STP. |
| **Solubility in water** | ~0.0006 mol L⁻¹ at 25 °C | Very low solubility. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series | Emission lines in UV and visible spectra. |
| **Common uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant, laboratory standard gas. | |

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, lowest density among gases.
- **Highly electronegative**: attracts electrons strongly.
- **Strongly reactive**: forms hydrides, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water.
- **Low boiling/melting points**: remains gaseous at room temperature.
- **Isotopic variants**: deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium in nuclear weapons and fusion reactors.
- **Key role in chemistry & energy**: fuels, catalysts, and as a probe in spectroscopy.

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, enabling its widespread use in industry, energy, and scientific research.
